title: Readiness 1 · Values through collections
prompt: Write two methods. public static int FinalCount(int start, List<int> changes) starts from start, adds every change that is 0 or more, and ignores negative changes. An empty list returns start. public static double AverageChange(List<int> changes) returns the average of all the changes, negative ones included, keeping any fraction. An empty list returns 0.
hints: Keep a running total. Where does it begin in each method?
FinalCount needs a test inside its loop. AverageChange needs a division that keeps its fraction.
In AverageChange, return 0 for an empty list, add the changes into a double, and divide by Count.
checkLabels: With no changes, FinalCount must return the start.
Changes of 0 must leave the count at 0.
Negative changes must be ignored: 2, 1 and 4 give 7.
Only negative changes must leave the start unchanged.
The average of 1 and 2 must be 1.5.
The average of no changes must be 0.
Negative changes count in the average: -4 and 4 give 0.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Adds negative changes to the count.
Divides two ints, so the average loses its fraction.

feedback: Compare an empty list, a list of zeros and a mix of positive and negative changes. For the average, check the types on both sides of the division.
